ops.title: Task anchors: three flags on add, the full octet on edit — and why the branch anchor stayed
ops.body:
Settled 2026-07-27, after one reversal. Records the reversal because the losing argument is the one a future reader will re-invent.

**The shipped surface.** `task add --commit/--path/--dir`; `task edit` takes the full standard octet including `--add-branch`/`--rm-branch`. `task` joins `TestAnchoredKindsUniform` for both the add group (trio) and the edit group (octet), with one machine-pinned exception: `TestTaskAddBranchIsTheBranchAttribute` asserts `task add --branch` remains the scalar `Task.Branch` LWW attribute.

**Why `task add` cannot take `--branch`.** `internal/cli/task.go:243` already binds it as the task's first-class branch attribute, mutually exclusive with `--backlog`. The shared anchor binder `anchorSets.bind` (`internal/cli/flags.go:61`) registers `--commit/--path/--dir/--branch` as StringArrays, so binding both on one command is a pflag redefinition panic at construction — not a style question. `task edit` has no such collision: it binds bare `--branch`/`--backlog`, and the `--add-*`/`--rm-*` octet is free.

**The reversal.** The orchestrator first ruled out branch anchors on tasks entirely — three kinds on both verbs — on the grounds that a branch anchor plus `Task.Branch` hands the graph builder two sources for one edge, forcing a precedence rule between an LWW scalar and a set-valued anchor, or silent double-counting. That argument is real but small, and it loses to two things once you look at the code:

1. **Deduplication is one line.** The graph builder unions `Task.Branch` with any branch-kind anchors into a set. There is no precedence to decide because the edge is the same edge; it is a set-membership question, not a conflict.
2. **The alternative costs more surface irregularity than it saves.** Dropping `--add-branch`/`--rm-branch` would leave task with six of the eight standard edit flags, requiring a second, less principled exception in `TestAnchoredKindsUniform` — one that could only be explained as "because we did not want this capability", where the add-group exception explains itself as "the name is taken." That test exists precisely to stop the anchor surface drifting per-kind, and the shipped shape lets it cover task for both verbs.

**Standing rule for the graph builder:** when materializing branch edges for a task, union `Task.Branch` with branch-kind anchors and deduplicate. Do not treat them as competing sources, and do not emit two edges.

**Two things the same work established, both cheaper than budgeted.** No new op kind was needed — `AddAnchor`/`RemoveAnchor` and `applyAnchor` are already kind-agnostic. And commit `a467728` (runbook anchors) is an exact precedent for the storage-format handling: `Anchors []Anchor` with `omitempty` as the last field, `sortedAnchorsNil` in the folder so anchor-less task snapshots stay byte-identical, `CreateTask.Anchors` on the op, and the pre-anchor `create_task` wire bytes re-pinned decode-side. The `checkpoint_task` golden did not move.

**One render collision:** `renderTaskShow` already prints `commits` (the `LinkCommit` set) and `branch`, so the text renderer prefixes the anchor block `anchor_commits`/`anchor_paths`/`anchor_dirs`/`anchor_branches`. JSON has no collision and uses the standard `anchors` array.
